text: Taylor Harry Fritz, born on 28 October 1997, is an American professional tennis player with a career-high singles ranking of world No. 4, achieved on 18 November 2024, and a best doubles ranking of No. 104, reached on 26 July 2021. He has won ten ATP Tour singles titles, including a Masters 1000 title at the 2022 Indian Wells Open, and was a finalist at the 2024 US Open and the 2024 ATP Finals. Fritz won a junior major singles title at the 2015 US Open and was the runner-up in junior singles at the 2015 French Open. He reached his first ATP Tour final in his third career event, the 2016 Memphis Open. He is the youngest of three boys, born to Kathy May, a former top-10 WTA player, and Guy Henry Fritz, who played professional tennis and was named US Olympic Development Coach of the Year in 2016; they divorced when he was 18. Through his mother, he is the great-great-grandson of David May, founder of The May Department Stores Company, which merged with Macy's. Fritz has two older maternal half-brothers, Chris and Kyle, and his uncle, Harry Fritz, also played professional tennis and won the longest Davis Cup match in history by number of games. His aunt, Laura Fritz, was a competitive swimmer who reached a top-5 world ranking in the 100 freestyle and was part of the world record 400 X4 freestyle relay team. Fritz grew up in Rancho Santa Fe in the San Diego metropolitan area with his brothers and attended Torrey Pines High School, where he won the CIF singles title in the San Diego section as a freshman. He switched to an online high school during his sophomore year to play full-time ITF junior events. He did not play any ITF events until he was 15, when he competed in a Grade-4 tournament in March 2013 in Clairemont. He began competing regularly on the ITF Circuit at the 2013 Junior US Open, shortly before turning 16, and reached the semifinals at the 2014 Junior Wimbledon tournament. He won his first Grade A tournament at the 2014 Osaka Mayor's Cup. In 2015, he reached at least the quarterfinal of all four junior Grand Slam tournaments, including the final at the French Open where he lost to Tommy Paul and the final at the US Open where he defeated Paul, finishing the year as the number-one-ranked boy's junior tennis player and being named the 2015 ITF Junior World Champion—making him the first American to hold the title since Donald Young in 2005 and Andy Roddick in 2000. He played his first ATP Tour tournament at Nottingham, where he received a wild card and won his first ATP match against Pablo Carreño Busta. In September 2015, after winning the Junior US Open, he turned pro and quickly rose from the 600s into the top 250 of the ATP rankings by becoming the 9th player at age 17 to win multiple Challenger Tour titles in back-to-back weeks, joining Top 20 players Bernard Tomic, Tomáš Berdych, Richard Gasquet, and Juan Martín del Potro, as well as Number 1 players Rafael Nadal and Novak Djokovic. After losing in the final of his last tournament in 2015, he reached a final again in his first tournament of 2016, winning against top-100 player Dudi Sela at Happy Valley to reach the 150s in the rankings. He advanced through Australian Open Qualifying to reach his first main draw of a Grand Slam tournament at the Australian Open, where he lost in the first round to Jack Sock in five sets. He was awarded a wildcard into his first ATP 250 tournament of 2016 at Memphis, where he defeated second-seeded Steve Johnson, the highest-ranked player he had ever defeated, and then beat Ričardas Berankis in the semifinal to become the youngest American to reach an ATP final since Michael Chang in 1988 and the second-fastest American to reach an ATP final, doing so in just his third career ATP tournament, behind only John Isner. He lost in the final to Kei Nishikori. In February 2016, he cracked the top 100 for the first time by reaching the quarterfinals in Acapulco at his first ATP 500 event. His grass-court season was highlighted by a close three-set loss to Roger Federer at Stuttgart, and he peaked in the rankings at No. 53 toward the end of the summer. At the US Open, he drew Jack Sock in the first round for the second time that year and lost in five sets. He won the ATP Star of Tomorrow award in 2016 for being the youngest player in the top 100 at age 19. In 2017, he achieved his first victory over a top-10 ATP player at Indian Wells, defeating sixth seed Marin Čilić in the second round. He struggled with injuries in the first half of the year and skipped the clay court season to recover. He returned in the summer with quarterfinals at Los Cabos and Winston-Salem. In his seventh Grand Slam appearance, he won his first match at a major by defeating Marcos Baghdatis at the US Open before losing in the second round to Dominic Thiem. After finishing 2017 just outside the top 100, he had a strong start to 2018, reaching two Challenger finals in January. He returned to the Top 100 by reaching the final in New Caledonia, where he lost to Noah Rubin. After a loss in qualifying at the Australian Open, he won his first Challenger title in two years at the inaugural event in Newport Beach, near his current residence in Palos Verdes. He continued his strong start by reaching the fourth round at Indian Wells, his first round of 16 appearance at a Masters event. He began the clay-court season with a semifinals appearance at the US Men's Clay Court Championships in Houston, the best result on clay of his career, where he upset Ryan Harrison and Jack Sock before losing to Steve Johnson, helping him return to No. 66 in the world. At the US Open, he reached his first Grand Slam third round, defeating Mischa Zverev and Jason Kubler, before losing to 9th-seeded Dominic Thiem in four sets. Earlier in the season, he began working with Paul Annacone, who helped him reach a career-high ranking of world No. 47 on November 5, 2018. He made the third round at the Australian Open, losing to Roger Federer in three sets. He won the Challenger at Newport Beach, defeating Brayden Schnur of Canada in straight sets. In June, he won his first ATP Tour title at the Eastbourne International by defeating Sam Querrey in straight sets. In the first round of Wimbledon, he defeated Tomáš Berdych in straight sets before losing to Jan-Lennard Struff in four sets. At the US Open, he was seeded 26th, his first-ever Grand Slam seeding, but lost in the first round to Feliciano López. He represented Team World in the third annual Laver Cup in Geneva. In his first singles match, he lost to Stefanos Tsitsipas, but bounced back on the final day by defeating Dominic Thiem. At the Swiss Indoors, he defeated 2nd-seeded Alexander Zverev in the first round in straight sets. After achieving a career-high ranking of world No. 25 on August 5, 2019, he ended the year ranked No. 32 in the world. He began his 2020 season at the inaugural ATP Cup, representing Team USA, going 1–2 in singles and being eliminated in the round-robin stage. At the Australian Open, he reached the third round with a five-set victory over Kevin Anderson before losing to Dominic Thiem. He reached his first ATP 500 final in Acapulco, where he lost to Rafael Nadal, and this runner-up finish propelled him to a new career-high ranking of world No. 24 on March 2, 2020. At the US Open, he was seeded 19th, defeated Dominik Koepfer in four sets, beat Gilles Simon in the second round, and lost to Denis Shapovalov in the third round in five sets. At the French Open, he was seeded 27th, defeated Tomáš Macháč in five sets and Radu Albot in straight sets before losing to Lorenzo Sonego in the third round in straight sets. The match against Sonego had the longest tie-break in French Open history, with Fritz losing 17–19. He started his 2021 season at the first edition of the Murray River Open, seeded sixth, reaching the third round before losing to Jérémy Chardy. Seeded 27th at the Australian Open, he reached the third round, where he was defeated by top seed, eight-time champion, and eventual champion Novak Djokovic in five sets, despite coming back from two sets to love down. In Doha, he reached the semifinals, defeating Lorenzo Sonego, sixth seed David Goffin, and fourth seed Denis Shapovalov before losing to Nikoloz Basilashvili. Seeded 15th at the Dubai Championships, he defeated Basilashvili in the second round in three sets, and was beaten in the third round by second seed Andrey Rublev. Seeded 22nd at the Miami Open, he reached the fourth round, losing to 32nd seed Alexander Bublik, which was his best showing at the event and only his second fourth-round appearance at a Masters 1000. He dropped out of the top 30 on May 10, 2021, after first-round losses at Monte-Carlo and Madrid, marking the first time no American men were in the Top 30 in nearly half a century. At the 2021 French Open, he was seeded 30th, defeated João Sousa in the first round in straight sets, and suffered a torn meniscus during a 4-set loss to Dominik Koepfer. After surgery, he returned in time for Wimbledon and reached the third round, where he lost to Alexander Zverev. At the 2021 BNP Paribas Open, he earned his first top 10 win in two years by beating world No. 7 and 5th seed Matteo Berrettini to reach the second fourth round at a Masters 1000, only the third in his career. It was his first win against a Top-10 opponent in 2021 and the seventh of his career. He then beat 10th seed Jannik Sinner to advance to his first Masters 1000 quarterfinal. There, he saved two match points to earn his biggest win of the year, defeating world No. 4 and 3rd seed Alexander Zverev to reach his first Masters 1000 semifinal, where he lost to Nikoloz Basilashvili. At the 2021 St. Petersburg Open, he turned 24 and won against countryman Tommy Paul, reaching the final where he lost to Marin Čilić. At the 2021 Rolex Paris Masters, he reached his second Masters 1000 quarterfinal, defeating Lorenzo Sonego, 5th seed and world No. 6 Andrey Rublev, and 10th seed and Indian Wells champion Cameron Norrie, for his third Top-10 win of the year and 10th Top-10 win of his career. He lost to Novak Djokovic in the quarterfinals. With this successful run, he reached a new career-high ranking in the top 25 at world No. 23 and became the No. 1 American player in singles on November 8, 2021. He ended the year ranked 23. Fritz started his 2022 season by representing the U.S. at the ATP Cup, where the U.S. was in Group C with Canada, Great Britain, and Germany. He defeated Félix Auger-Aliassime of Canada and Cameron Norrie of Great Britain but lost to Alexander Zverev of Germany, resulting in the U.S. finishing fourth in Group C. Seeded 20th at the Australian Open, he reached the second week of a Grand Slam for the first time after defeating 15th seed Roberto Bautista Agut in the third round in five sets. He fell in the fourth round to fourth seed Stefanos Tsitsipas in five sets, making his debut in the top 20 of the singles rankings on January 31. As the top seed at the Dallas Open, he reached the quarterfinals, where he was eliminated by seventh seed and compatriot Marcos Giron. Seeded seventh in Acapulco, he lost in the second round to qualifier Yoshihito Nishioka. Representing the U.S. in the Davis Cup tie against Colombia, he played one match and beat Alejandro González, helping the U.S. win 4–0 to make up for a previous loss to Colombia. Seeded 20th in Indian Wells, he became the first American to reach the final at the event since John Isner in 2012 by defeating 29th seed Alex de Minaur in the fourth round, Miomir Kecmanović in the quarterfinals, and seventh seed Andrey Rublev in the semifinals. He then defeated fourth seed, three-time champion, and then-21 Grand Slam champion Rafael Nadal in the final in straight sets, claiming his maiden Masters 1000 title, his second career ATP title, and ending Nadal's 20-match winning streak. It was his first win over a member of the Big Three in nine career matches and marked the first time an American man had won the Indian Wells title since Andre Agassi in 2001. This victory marked his top 15 debut and reached a career-high ranking of No. 13. Seeded 11th at the Miami Open, he entered the tournament aiming to complete the Sunshine Double but lost in the fourth round to Miomir Kecmanović in three sets. He started his clay-court season at the U.S. Clay Court Championships in Houston, Texas, seeded second, reaching the quarterfinals before losing to fifth seed and 2019 champion Cristian Garín. Seeded 10th at the Monte-Carlo Masters, he lost in the quarterfinals to eventual finalist Alejandro Davidovich Fokina. He missed the Madrid Open and Italian Open due to a left foot injury. Seeded 13th at the French Open, he was defeated in the second round by qualifier Bernabé Zapata Miralles. He began his grass-court season at the Libéma Open, seeded third, suffering a second-round upset to Dutch wildcard and eventual champion Tim van Rijthoven. Seeded fourth at the Queen's Club Championships, he was eliminated in the first round by British wildcard Jack Draper. Seeded third at the Eastbourne International, he beat sixth seed and defending champion Alex de Minaur in the semifinals to reach the final for the first time since 2019 when he won the title. He defeated compatriot Maxime Cressy in the final to win his third ATP Tour title and second in Eastbourne. Seeded 11th at Wimbledon, he defeated Alex Molčan and qualifier Jason Kubler in the third and fourth rounds respectively to reach his first Major quarterfinal. In the quarterfinals, he pushed world No. 4, second seed, and two-time champion Rafael Nadal to five sets but lost in a fifth-set tiebreak. His American swing began in Washington, where he was the third seed. After defeating Alexei Popyrin in straight sets, he retired against Dan Evans in the third round due to the heat, despite having a match point in the second set. At the Canada Masters, he beat Andy Murray and Frances.

At the Eastbourne International, seeded third, Fritz reached the final by defeating sixth seed and defending champion Alex de Minaur in the semifinals, marking his first final appearance since 2019 when he won the title; he then defeated compatriot Maxime Cressy to win his third ATP Tour title and second in Eastbourne. Seeded 11th at Wimbledon, he advanced to his first Major quarterfinal by defeating Alex Molčan and qualifier Jason Kubler in the third and fourth rounds, but lost in a five-set match to world No. 4 and second seed Rafael Nadal in the quarterfinals. In Washington, as the third seed, he beat Alexei Popyrin in straight sets before retiring against Dan Evans in the third round due to heat, despite having a match point in the second set; at the Canada Masters, he defeated Andy Murray and Frances Tiafoe before losing to Evans in three sets. In Cincinnati, he reached the quarterfinals by defeating Sebastián Báez, Nick Kyrgios, and sixth seed Andrey Rublev, but lost to world No. 1 Daniil Medvedev; at the US Open, he suffered a first-round defeat to first-time qualifier Brandon Holt, who earned his first ATP Tour win. Fritz withdrew from the Korea Open due to COVID-19 but reached his second ATP 500 final in Tokyo, where, as the third seed, he beat James Duckworth, Hiroki Moriya, received a walkover from Nick Kyrgios, and defeated Denis Shapovalov; he defeated Tiafoe in straight sets to become the first American champion since Pete Sampras in 1996, reaching a career-high ranking of World No. 8 on October 10, 2022, the first American to crack the Top 10 since Jack Sock in 2017. At the Paris Masters, he won against Alejandro Davidovich Fokina in the first round before losing to French wildcard Gilles Simon in a three-set match lasting 3 hours and 5 minutes, missing qualification for the 2022 ATP Finals but becoming an alternate; after Carlos Alcaraz’s withdrawal due to injury, Fritz qualified for the 2022 ATP Finals, the first American since John Isner in 2018; in the round robin, he defeated Rafael Nadal on his debut, his first win over a top-3 player, lost to Casper Ruud, and defeated Félix Auger-Aliassime to reach the semifinals, the first American since Jack Sock in 2017 to reach that stage, marking his 45th tour-level win of the season; he lost to Novak Djokovic in straight sets. Fritz finished the year ranked inside the top-10 for the first time, at world No. 9. At the inaugural 2023 United Cup, as the No. 1 American male player, the United States team won the championship by defeating Italy in the final; at the Australian Open, he lost in the second round to wildcard Alexei Popyrin, saving a match point in the fourth set to make it two sets all, but lost a match lasting over four hours. At the 2023 Dallas Open, he reached the semifinals, losing to Wu Yibing, and reached a new career-high ranking of world No. 7, the highest ranked American since Mardy Fish in 2011; as the top seed, he reached back-to-back semifinals at the 2023 Delray Beach Open, defeated Mackenzie McDonald to reach his first ATP final of the season and tenth overall, and defeated Miomir Kecmanović to win his fifth ATP Tour title, moving to world No. 5 on February 27, 2023. At the Mexican Open, he defeated Frances Tiafoe to reach his third straight semifinal, losing to Tommy Paul in an epic match lasting three and a half hours, setting a record for the longest match in the 30-year history of the Abierto Mexicano Telcel. In Indian Wells and Miami, he reached back-to-back quarterfinals by defeating Sebastián Báez, Márton Fucsovics, and Denis Shapovalov, Holger Rune respectively. In Monte Carlo, he reached his third consecutive Masters quarterfinal by defeating Stan Wawrinka and Jiří Lehečka, then defeated two-time defending champion Stefanos Tsitsipas to reach the semifinals, recording his 200th win and becoming the first American in 20 years to reach the semifinals at this Masters since Vince Spadea; he lost in three sets to Andrey Rublev after winning the first set. Seeded second at the 2023 BMW Open, he reached the semifinals with wins over Márton Fucsovics and Dominic Thiem; in Madrid, he lost to Zhizhen Zhang after Zhang saved three match points to reach the quarterfinals; in Rome, he lost in the second round to qualifier Yannick Hanfmann. He won his sixth title at the 2023 Atlanta Open by defeating Aleksandar Vukic; at the US Open, he reached the quarterfinals for the first time at a Major but lost to Novak Djokovic. At the 2023 Japan Open, as the defending champion, he lost to wildcard Shintaro Mochizuki after being a set up and serving at 5–2 in the third set. Seeded fifth in Basel, he lost to Alexander Shevchenko after missing 15 break point opportunities in a match lasting nearly three hours with three tiebreaks; in Paris, he withdrew before the second round due to injury, ending the season early, though potentially remaining as an alternate at the 2023 ATP Finals. He reached his first quarterfinal at the Australian Open by defeating Stefanos Tsitsipas in four sets; he successfully defended his Delray Beach title by defeating Tommy Paul; at the 2024 Miami Open, he lost in the second round to qualifier Thiago Seyboth Wild, having received a bye. He had a successful start to the clay season at the Bavarian International Tennis Championships in Munich, reaching his first clay court final by defeating Cristian Garín and regaining the American No. 1 ranking; at the 2024 Mutua Madrid Open, he reached his second clay Masters quarterfinal and tenth overall, defeating Luciano Darderi, Sebastián Báez, and Hubert Hurkacz, his second top-10 career win on clay; he defeated Francisco Cerúndolo for his 250th career win, becoming the sixth man born in 1995 or later to reach that milestone and the first American man to reach the semifinals of Madrid since it switched to clay in 2009 and the third after Andre Agassi and Robby Ginepri; at the 2024 Italian Open, he reached back-to-back quarterfinals by defeating Fabio Fognini, Sebastian Korda, and Grigor Dimitrov, becoming the first American man to reach the quarterfinals or better at all three clay court Masters tournaments; it was also the first time multiple American players (with Tommy Paul) reached the quarterfinals in Rome since 2008; at the 2024 French Open, he reached the fourth round of a clay Major for the first time with a five-set win over Thanasi Kokkinakis. Seeded third, he reached the Paris Olympics semifinals with Tommy Paul and won the bronze medal by defeating the Czech duo Tomáš Macháč and Adam Pavlásek. Seeded 12th at the US Open, Fritz reached his first Grand Slam semifinal by defeating Camilo Ugo Carabelli, Matteo Berrettini, Francisco Comesaña, Casper Ruud, and Alexander Zverev, his first two consecutive top-10 wins in a Major; he became the first American since Andre Agassi in 2001 to reach the fourth round at each Grand Slam in the same season; by reaching the semifinals, he set up an all-American matchup with Frances Tiafoe, the first at a Grand Slam since 2005 at the US Open; he won the match in five sets to reach his first Grand Slam final, but lost to Jannik Sinner in straight sets; in an interview on the Nothing Major podcast, he admitted the emotional toll of the loss. At the ATP Finals in November, Fritz reached the semifinals after two wins and one loss in the group stages, beating Daniil Medvedev and Alex De Minaur; he defeated Alexander Zverev in the semifinals to reach his first final at the end-of-season event, becoming the first American to reach the championship match at the ATP Finals since James Blake in 2006; he lost the final to Jannik Sinner in straight sets; despite the loss, he ended the season with a new career-high singles ranking of world No. 4 on November 18. Opening the year as a career-high No. 4 in the world rankings, Fritz helped the United States win the United Cup title, their second in three years, winning four of five matches over Borna Coric, Zhizhen Zhang, Tomas Machac, and Hubert Hurkacz. Entering the 2025 Australian Open as the fourth seed, he cruised through his first two matches, dropping only 8 games against Jenson Brooksby and Christian Garin, but lost in four sets to Gael Monfils, marking his earliest exit at a Grand Slam since the 2023 Wimbledon Championships. After disappointing early exits in Delray Beach and Dallas, Fritz entered Indian Wells aiming to recapture his 2022 win; he reached the fourth round for the fifth straight time but lost to Jack Draper in straight sets. Entering the Miami Open as the third seed, aiming for his second ATP 1000 title, he reached the quarterfinals for the second time after defeating Lorenzo Sonego, Denis Shapovalov, and Adam Walton; in the quarterfinal, he defeated Matteo Berrettini in three sets to reach his first semifinal at the tournament; in the semifinal, he lost a close three-set match to eventual champion Jakub Menšík. During the 2025 grass season, Fritz won two titles: the BOSS Open after a fifth straight victory over Alexander Zverev, and the Eastbourne International, defeating Jenson Brooksby in the final. At Wimbledon, he defeated Karen Khachanov to reach the semifinals for the first time in that tournament, becoming the first American man to do so since John Isner in 2018; he lost to Carlos Alcaraz in four sets. At the US Open, he reached the quarterfinals and lost to Novak Djokovic in four sets. At the 2025 Japan Open in Tokyo, he reached the final and lost to world No. 1 Carlos Alcaraz, who avenged his loss at the 2025 Laver Cup, where team World defeated team Europe. At the 2025 Rolex Shanghai Masters, he reached the third round, recording his 50th win of the season, becoming the first American in 20 years to reach that milestone and to do so in three consecutive seasons (54 in 2023, 53 in 2024) since Andy Roddick. Since early 2024, Fritz wears Hugo Boss clothing on court, previously sponsored by Nike; he uses ASICS Gel-Resolution tennis shoes and a Head Radical MP racquet. He has partnerships with Motorola, Eight Sleep, La Roche Posay, and Chipotle Mexican Grill. Fritz is an offensive baseliner with powerful, penetrating groundstrokes that force errors or end points as winners; his most consistent stroke is his forehand, and he has a strong, flatter backhand; though not comfortable at the net, he has significantly improved his net game and movement. Standing 6 feet 5 inches (1.96 meters) tall, he has a dominant serve reaching 149 miles per hour (240 km/h) and solid groundstrokes off both wings; he uses an almost full-western grip on his forehand, bordering on Hawaiian, a defining aspect of his style; he excels at sharp angle cross-court shots on both sides and has a good topspin lob. He has a son, Jordan (born in 2017), with former pro tennis player Raquel Pedraza, whom he married from 2016 to 2019. Fritz is an avid player of World of Warcraft and Rust, and occasionally live streams his gaming on Twitch under the name TaylorFritz97. Since June 2020, he has been in a relationship with fashion influencer Morgan Riddle. He appeared in the tennis docuseries Break Point, which premiered on Netflix on January 13, 2023 and concluded in 2024. Fritz has played three seasons with World TeamTennis, making his debut in 2015 with the San Diego Aviators, playing two additional seasons with them in 2018 and 2019; he joined the Philadelphia Freedoms in 2020 at The Greenbrier, advancing to the WTT Playoffs as the No. 1 seed but losing to the New York Empire in the semifinal; he was named the WTT 2020 Male MVP. Current through the 2025 US Open.
